test_title: PYST 7: RRB Group D - GA (Held On: 01 Dec, 2025 Shift 1)
subject: general
question: On 20th May, 2025, the Supreme Court (SC) reinstated the requirement of how many years of legal practice for law graduates to apply for civil judge (junior division) posts, reversing its 2002 decision?
solution:
The correct answer is __**3 years**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• On **20th May, 2025**, the Supreme Court of India reinstated the requirement of **3 years** of legal practice for law graduates to apply for the posts of **Civil Judge (Junior Division).**
 
• This decision reversed a previous ruling made by the Supreme Court in **2002**, which had allowed fresh law graduates to directly apply for these judicial posts without any mandatory legal practice.
 
• The **3-year legal practice requirement** ensures that candidates gain adequate exposure and experience in the field of law before assuming judicial responsibilities.
 
• The move aligns with the objective of enhancing the quality of judicial appointments and ensuring that candidates have substantial practical knowledge of legal proceedings.
 
• The Supreme Court emphasized the importance of practical experience in law to ensure candidates are well-prepared to handle judicial duties effectively. ***Hence, the correct answer is 3 years.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Supreme Court's 2002 Decision:**

 
 
• In **2002**, the Supreme Court allowed law graduates to apply for Civil Judge posts without requiring prior legal practice.
 
• This decision was aimed at increasing the pool of candidates for judicial posts and fast-tracking appointments.
 
 
 
• **Importance of Legal Practice:**
 
 
• Legal practice enables candidates to gain **hands-on experience** in court proceedings, drafting, arguing cases, and understanding nuances of legal processes.
 
• It also helps candidates develop critical thinking, analytical skills, and familiarity with judicial ethics and responsibilities.
 
 
 
• **Eligibility for Civil Judge (Junior Division):**
 
 
• Eligibility criteria include a **Bachelor’s degree in law (LLB)** from a recognized institution.
 
• Post the Supreme Court’s 2025 ruling, candidates must have **3 years of legal practice** as a prerequisite.
 
• Age limits and other criteria may vary across states in India.
 
 
 
• **Significance of Judicial Appointments:**
 
 
• Judicial appointments play a critical role in ensuring **efficient administration of justice**.
 
• Experienced and well-trained judges contribute to maintaining the quality, impartiality, and integrity of the judiciary.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Supreme Court's Role:**

 
 
• The Supreme Court of India is the **highest judicial authority** in the country and has the power to interpret laws and review its previous decisions.
 
• It plays a pivotal role in ensuring justice and upholding the **Constitution of India.**
 
 
 
• **Judicial Ethics and Experience:**
 
 
• Judicial ethics demand fairness, impartiality, and adherence to legal principles.
 
• Practical legal experience equips candidates with skills to manage complex cases and deliver unbiased decisions.
 
 
 
• **Impact of the Decision:**
 
 
• The reinstatement of the **3-year legal practice requirement** aims to enhance the competency of Civil Judges (Junior Division).
 
• It ensures that candidates have sufficient exposure to real-world legal challenges before taking on judicial roles.
